Title: Archive Explorer
Description: Open ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ and Zstandard or Brotli archives in the browser, list their contents, extract selected files safely and create new ZIP or TAR archives.

Seo_Introduction: Archive Explorer opens ZIP, TAR and compressed TAR archives (gzip, Zstandard, Brotli) directly in the browser. It lists every entry with its size, compressed size, date and method, extracts the files you select into a folder or a new ZIP, and packs your own files into ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ or TAR.ZST. Nothing is uploaded.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
A ZIP is read from its central directory, including ZIP64 archives, self-extracting stubs and Info-ZIP Unicode names, so even an archive with a million entries opens without unpacking it. TAR archives are read header by header with GNU long names and pax records; a compressed TAR is unpacked in one streaming pass in a Web Worker. Deflate, gzip, Zstandard and Brotli run in WASM with a bounded output window, so a compression bomb never inflates more than 1 MiB at a time.

Extraction is guarded against path traversal (Zip Slip): absolute paths, drive letters, “..” segments and control characters are never written, symlinks and hard links are never created, and characters or device names Windows refuses are replaced. Each entry must match its declared size and CRC-32; overlapping entries, ratios above 1000:1 past 64 MiB and output beyond 64 GiB stop the extraction. In Chromium-based browsers files go straight into a folder you pick, keeping existing files; elsewhere the selection downloads as one ZIP.

Creating an archive streams each file through the compressor to the file you save, with UTF-8 names, ZIP64 for files of 4 GiB and more, and pax headers for long TAR names.
Seo_Examples:
**Look inside a download:** open a 2 GB release.zip to see its 40,000 files and their sizes in a second, without unpacking it.

**Pull one log out of a backup:** filter a logs.tar.gz by “2026-10”, select the matching files and extract only them to a folder.

**Check a suspicious archive:** a ZIP whose entries contain “../../etc/passwd” is listed with those entries marked as unsafe, and they are never written.

**Pack a project folder:** add a folder, choose TAR.ZST at level 3, and save a compressed archive that keeps the folder structure.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Open an archive
Drop or choose a ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ, TAR.ZST, TAR.BR, GZ, ZST or BR file. The list of entries appears when reading finishes.

### Step 2: Find and select files
Type part of a name in Filter, then click rows or use Select matching. Selecting a folder selects everything inside it.

### Step 3: Extract
Choose Extract to folder… in Chromium-based browsers, Download as ZIP anywhere, or Save the file when one file is selected.

### Step 4: Create an archive
Add files or a folder under Create archive, choose a format and level, and save the new archive.
Seo_Tips:
- A single .gz, .zst or .br file without TAR inside appears as one entry; its size is known only after extraction.
- Encrypted ZIP entries and methods such as BZIP2, LZMA or Deflate64 are listed but not extracted.
- Cancel stops the worker at once; a partially written file is discarded.
- To compare how gzip, Brotli and Zstandard handle your data, try Compression Benchmark.
